key_facts: The Chair called the meeting to order and mentioned that today's proceedings will be televised.
The Chair proceeded to ministerial announcements, but there were none.
Mr. Paul Manly presented a petition calling for a ban on cosmetic testing using animals, following the European Union model.
Hon. Pierre Poilievre tabled an e-petition regarding mandatory life jackets for children under 14 on small vessels.
Hon. Pierre Poilievre asked the Prime Minister if the government instructed public servants to ignore red flags of fraudulent cases.
The Prime Minister stated that the priority was getting money to Canadians quickly and that fraudsters will have to repay the money they received.
Mr. Yves-Franois Blanchet questioned the Prime Minister about the employment incentives accompanying the Canada emergency response benefit.
The Prime Minister mentioned programs like Canada summer jobs and another program with 76,000 new jobs for young people.
Mr. Jagmeet Singh questioned the Prime Minister about the federal government's responsibility in addressing the impact of the pandemic on seniors.
The Prime Minister stated that the federal government respects provincial jurisdiction and will support provinces in managing long-term care facilities.
Mr. Jagmeet Singh asked if the Prime Minister would commit to removing profit from the long-term care system.
The Prime Minister acknowledged the need to improve care for seniors and mentioned working with provinces to address long-term care improvements.
Hon. Pierre Poilievre asked how many emergency response benefit cheques were sent to people flagged as fraudulent.
Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos stated that 7.7 million Canadians received the Canada emergency response benefit.
Hon. Pierre Poilievre questioned if 200,000 cheques were sent to fraudulent applicants.
Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos clarified that approximately 7.7 million Canadians received at least one payment.
Hon. Pierre Poilievre asked how many prisoners received the cheques.
Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos stated that the benefit is an emergency measure and that the government is ensuring its integrity.
Hon. Pierre Poilievre mentioned the Auditor General is reducing audits due to lack of funding.
Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos stated that the government is supporting the Auditor General's work.
Hon. Pierre Poilievre asked if the government would give the Auditor General the funding he requested.
Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos stated that the government increased funding for the Auditor General.
Hon. Pierre Poilievre asked if the National Post's report about 200,000 fraudulent users was accurate.
Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos stated that the report was inaccurate and that the benefit was given to those who truly needed it.
Mr. Grard Deltell asked if the National Post's report about 200,000 fraudulent users was correct.
Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos stated that the report was incorrect and that the government has mechanisms to ensure integrity.
Mr. Grard Deltell asked what a person who received the full CERB and returned to work should do.
Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos stated that the person should contact Service Canada or the Canada Revenue Agency.
Mrs. Tracy Gray asked if the government would fix the CEBA program to include businesses that pay owner-operators through dividends.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government has shown flexibility in eligibility criteria.
Mrs. Tracy Gray mentioned that small business owners in her riding are ineligible for CEBA because they don't have a business account.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government decreased the payroll threshold for CEBA eligibility.
Mrs. Tracy Gray mentioned that the Canadian Craft Brewers Association reported that 38% of craft brewers did not qualify for the Canadian emergency wage subsidy in March.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the wage subsidy revenue threshold was changed from 30% to 15%.
Mr. John Barlow mentioned that a survey showed more than half of respondents have not qualified for any programs.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that 590,000 loans have been issued through the CEBA program.
Mr. John Barlow asked if the government would expand eligibility for some programs to include sole proprietorships.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government is working on being more generous with programs.
Mr. John Barlow asked about the impact of losing 30,000 family farms on food security and grocery prices.
Hon. Marie-Claude Bibeau stated that the agriculture sector is an essential service and that risk management programs are in place.
Mr. John Barlow asked about the availability of funds set aside for cattle and pork producers.
Hon. Marie-Claude Bibeau stated that additional money was added for the processing sector and pork and beef producers.
Mr. John Barlow asked about the carbon tax impact on agriculture.
Hon. Marie-Claude Bibeau stated that the government has provided various exemptions to the agriculture sector.
Mr. Pat Kelly asked if the government would fully fund the Office of the Auditor General.
Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos stated that the government increased funding for the Auditor General.
Mr. Pat Kelly asked why the government refused to name a permanent replacement for the deceased Auditor General.
Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos stated that the government supports Statistics Canada and is cooperating with investigations.
Mr. Pat Kelly asked about the estimated annual debt servicing cost of the aid measures.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the government is committed to supporting Canadians through the crisis.
Mr. Pat Kelly asked about the number of private sector bank loans funded under the business credit availability program.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the government is transparent with the finance committee about the numbers.
Mr. Pat Kelly asked about the dollar amount lent and guaranteed by Export Development Canada.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that over 550,000 loans were approved under the CEBA program, representing over 20 billion dollars.
Mr. Pat Kelly asked if the government would fix CEBA to include businesses that hire day labourers or subcontractors.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government is working to ensure more businesses can access the program.
Mr. Pat Kelly asked if the government would fix CEBA to include businesses that use personal chequing accounts.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the program has been well-received by many small businesses.
Hon. Michael Chong questioned the government about a leak of labor force survey data.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government is investigating the leak and ensuring proper procedures are followed.
Hon. Michael Chong asked if the government would notify the RCMP about the leak.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government is not prejudging the outcome of the investigation.
Mr. Yves-Franois Blanchet asked if health is in the exclusive jurisdiction of the provinces.
Hon. Patty Hajdu stated that the federal government transfers money to provinces to deliver healthcare, which is within their jurisdiction.
Mr. Yves-Franois Blanchet asked if there would be a permanent increase in health transfers without conditions.
Hon. Pablo Rodriguez stated that both official languages have the same value and importance.
Mrs. Marilne Gill asked about specific assistance for the seasonal tourism and fishing industries.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government has introduced measures to support the tourism and seasonal industries.
Mrs. Marilne Gill asked if the government would allow the Canada emergency response benefit to provide eligibility for employment insurance benefits.
Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos stated that the government has provided broader investments to support businesses and workers.
Mr. Jagmeet Singh asked about the limits on CEO bonuses and share buybacks in the business bailout.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the government will not allow share buybacks and will limit CEO compensation.
Mr. Jagmeet Singh asked if the government would deny public help to companies hiding money in offshore tax havens.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the government will not allow companies convicted of tax evasion to access funds.
Mr. Jagmeet Singh asked if companies not convicted of tax evasion but avoiding taxes would receive help.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the government is working with other countries to tighten international rules.
Mr. Randy Hoback asked about the eligibility of small businesses for the wage subsidy.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government has lowered the revenue threshold for the wage subsidy.
Mr. Randy Hoback asked about the approval of Canadian-made disinfectants.
Hon. Patty Hajdu stated that the government has accelerated the approval process for Canadian products.
Mr. Randy Hoback asked about the government's support for farmers.
Hon. Marie-Claude Bibeau stated that the government has announced specific programs for the meat sector.
Mr. Blaine Calkins asked about the opening of national parks in coordination with provincial parks.
Hon. Chrystia Freeland stated that the government is working with provincial partners on the reopening of parks.
Mr. Blaine Calkins asked about the postponement of lock operations in heritage waterways.
Hon. Chrystia Freeland stated that the government is working on coordinating national and provincial parks.
Mr. Blaine Calkins asked about the government's use of the pandemic to bypass democratic values.
Hon. Pablo Rodriguez stated that the government is meeting regularly and that the number of question periods is normal.
Mr. Blaine Calkins asked about the discrepancy in support for different economic sectors.
Hon. Marie-Claude Bibeau stated that the government is committed to all sectors, including agriculture and energy.
Mr. Blaine Calkins asked about the prohibition of the nine o'clock gun.
Hon. Bill Blair stated that the nine o'clock gun is not a prohibited firearm.
Mr. John Nater asked about the government's support for agricultural societies cancelling fall fairs.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government has increased funding for regional development agencies.
Mr. John Nater asked about the government's support for the arts and culture industry.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government has allocated $500 million to support arts, heritage, and sports organizations.
Mr. John Nater asked about the criteria for reopening international borders.
Hon. Chrystia Freeland stated that the health and safety of Canadians is the primary criterion for reopening borders.
Mr. John Nater asked about the government's support for people falling through the cracks in programs.
Hon. Jean-Yves Duclos stated that the government has measures in place to help those in difficult circumstances.
Mr. John Nater asked about the government's plan to address processing capacity issues in the beef and pork sectors.
Hon. Marie-Claude Bibeau stated that the government has increased advance payments for AgriStability.
Mr. Larry Maguire asked about the affordability of premiums for the western livestock price insurance program.
Hon. Marie-Claude Bibeau stated that the government has announced specific programs for the meat sector.
Mr. Larry Maguire asked about the eligibility of businesses like Chez Angela for the wage subsidy.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government has lowered the revenue threshold for the wage subsidy.
Mr. Larry Maguire asked about the ability to refinance loans through the Canada small business financing program.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government has deferred GST/HST and customs duty payments.
Mr. Larry Maguire asked about the government's stance on sport shooting competitions being illegal.
Hon. Bill Blair stated that the prohibited weapons are not used in Olympic or Paralympic Games.
Mr. Ben Lobb asked about the government's response to the Canadian Federation of Agriculture's request for an emergency fund.
Hon. Marie-Claude Bibeau stated that the government has a host of business risk management programs.
Mr. Ben Lobb asked about the carbon tax impact on pork farmers.
Hon. Marie-Claude Bibeau stated that the government has provided exemptions for agriculture.
Mr. Richard Lehoux asked about the government's plan to provide Internet access to rural areas.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government has launched a $1.7-billion program to support broadband infrastructure.
Mr. Richard Lehoux asked about the inclusion of general partnerships in the wage subsidy program.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government is considering the issue of general partnerships.
Mr. Tako Van Popta asked about the eligibility of dividend income for CEBA.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government is working with businesses to see how they can assist more Canadians.
Mr. Tako Van Popta asked about the government's support for small businesses stranded overseas.
Hon. Bill Blair stated that the government is considering each case on a case-by-case basis.
Mr. Tako Van Popta asked about the government's stance on the Alberta energy regulator suspending environmental monitoring.
Hon. Chrystia Freeland stated that Alberta has published draft regulations on methane.
Mr. Scott Duvall asked about the government's support for seniors.
Hon. Deb Schulte stated that the government has provided one-time tax-free payments to seniors.
Mr. Scott Duvall asked about the government's support for people with disabilities.
Hon. Deb Schulte stated that additional supports for other vulnerable Canadians are being considered.
Mr. Maxime Blanchette-Joncas asked about the effectiveness of the Canada emergency commercial rent assistance program.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the rent relief program is significant and more details will be available soon.
Mr. Maxime Blanchette-Joncas asked about the government's support for businesses covering the costs of new health measures.
Hon. Navdeep Bains stated that the government has invested $71 million in community futures development corporations.
Mr. Greg McLean asked about the design of the Canada emergency commercial rent assistance program.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the program is designed to help both landlords and tenants.
Mr. Greg McLean asked about the government's oil and gas policy and its impact on quantitative easing.
Hon. Chrystia Freeland stated that the government supports the oil and gas sector.
Mr. Greg McLean asked about the potential conflict of interest with BlackRock advising the Bank of Canada.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the Bank of Canada is independent from the government.
Mr. Pierre Poilievre asked about the total assets of the Government of Canada.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the spending on the Auditor General increased from 2014-15 to 2018-19.
Mr. Pierre Poilievre asked about the total liabilities of the Government of Canada.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the government is in a strong fiscal position.
Mr. Pierre Poilievre asked about the total national debt.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the government is making investments to support Canadians.
Mr. Pierre Poilievre asked about the total public and private debt in Canada.
Hon. Bill Morneau stated that the government is focused on supporting Canadians through the crisis.
